external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A customer who browses and places orders through the mobile app and receives a faxed confirmation.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application through which customers browse and order.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The API that receives app interactions, keeps customer data, hands orders to SIMS, and accepts catalogue changes.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system that processes orders, writes delivery addresses, and sends dispatch notes.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: The gateway that faxes dispatch confirmations to customers.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

processes.name: spreadsheet macros
processes.description: Macros in the marketing spreadsheet that send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: The database containing customer names, addresses, and paid card details.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: A file containing delivery addresses and nothing else.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else

data_stores.name: catalogue spreadsheet
data_stores.description: The spreadsheet containing the marketing catalogue, including prices and product copy.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.

data_stores.name: marketing laptop
data_stores.description: The office laptop where the catalogue spreadsheet lives.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: Customer browsing and ordering through the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: talks to
data_flows.description: The mobile app communicates with the web API over HTTP.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS

data_flows.name: keeps customers
data_flows.description: The web API keeps customer names, addresses, and paid card details in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
data_flows.data_description: customer names, addresses, and paid card details

data_flows.name: hands over order
data_flows.description: The web API hands an order to SIMS when an order is placed.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: writes address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address to the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: sends dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: faxes confirmation
data_flows.description: The fax gateway faxes a confirmation containing the customer's name and address.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

data_flows.name: changes catalogue
data_flows.description: Spreadsheet macros send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: The office location where the marketing laptop and catalogue spreadsheet are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The user database is confidential because it contains customer names, addresses, and paid card details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the user database contains customer names, addresses, and the card customers paid with.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file is confidential because it contains delivery addresses.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the flat file contains delivery addresses.

assumptions.assumption: The catalogue spreadsheet is confidential because it contains commercially sensitive prices and product copy.
assumptions.basis: The source states that macros change prices and product copy in the catalogue.

assumptions.assumption: The marketing laptop is confidential because it stores the catalogue spreadsheet containing prices and product copy.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the catalogue spreadsheet lives on the marketing laptop and contains prices and product copy.
